clue.text: When sent to Coventry, one that's barely seen?

definitions.text: When sent to Coventry, one that's barely seen?

parts.words: When sent to Coventry, one that's barely seen?
parts.note: 'sent to Coventry' usually means shunned, but here it is literal: the legendary noblewoman of Coventry rode through its streets naked, so she was barely (in the bare) seen

explanation.surface: Someone ostracised by colleagues becomes almost invisible.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'send someone to Coventry' is a British idiom for refusing to speak to them. Legend says the countess rode naked through Coventry while townsfolk kept their eyes shut.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary eleventh-century countess is famed for riding naked through Coventry, hence seen only in the bare.

clue.text: Reason Titanic captain might think the unthinkable?

definitions.text: Reason Titanic captain might think the unthinkable?

parts.words: Reason Titanic captain might think the unthinkable?
parts.note: the ship was called unsinkable; a speech impediment turning S into TH would make that word come out as 'unthinkable'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Think the unthinkable' sounds like bold planning, but the joke is pronunciation: with this impediment 'unsinkable' is said as 'unthinkable'.
explanation.definitionFit: A speech defect pronouncing S as TH is exactly what would turn the boast about the ship into a different word.

clue.text: Thawed, 99 disappearing — a performance

indicators.note: the 99 vanishes from the word, so those letters are taken out of it

parts.note: a thawed windscreen has been de-iced
IC is a crossword rendering of 99 in Roman numerals (100 less 1)

explanation.surface: An ice cream with a flake melting away as part of some show.
explanation.walkthrough: A '99' is a British ice-cream cone with a chocolate flake, which suits 'thawed'; here it is the Roman numeral IC.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed is an act or feat, something performed.

clue.text: Such a reduction applied to (s)quires?

parts.note: a paper cutter trims quires of paper, while the blade that beheads would take the head off squires, leaving quires

explanation.walkthrough: A quire is a set of sheets of paper, trimmed by a cutting machine of the same name as the execution device; beheading the S of squires gives quires.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting with the blade both trims stacks of paper and decapitates people, the two senses the bracketed S plays on.

clue.text: Aquatic being, part of Little Mermaid toy that's caught?

indicators.note: caught in the sense of heard by the ear, so the phrase is taken by sound

parts.note: a Little Mermaid toy is a doll with a fish tail, so part of it is the doll's fin

explanation.surface: A sea creature featured as part of a Little Mermaid playset that someone has fished out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' suggests fishing, but here it means caught by the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea mammal is a creature that lives in water.

clue.text: Seen as very absurd, runs off

indicators.note: the runs go off, departing from the word

parts.note: something absurd is laughable, risible

explanation.surface: Something regarded as utterly ridiculous, a reason to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything that can be seen is in plain view, perceptible to the eye.

clue.text: Train line almost flipped over vehicle

indicators.note: flipped over, so the shortened word is turned end to end
almost the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a railway line is a track

explanation.surface: A railway line nearly overturned by a passing vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cart is a wheeled conveyance, a simple vehicle often drawn by a horse.

clue.text: King overcome by slithering odious boa in stories that aren't to be read

definitions.text: stories that aren't to be read

indicators.note: the king is overwhelmed and held within the snake's coils, so his letter sits inside the rest
a slithering snake twists about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A monarch overpowered by a hateful snake, like something from a fairy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The scene suggests a story to be read; the definition says these stories are listened to instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Recorded narrations are books one listens to rather than reads.

clue.text: Entered private property: lock abruptly 'died'

indicators.note: cut off abruptly, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a lock of hair is a tress
passed is a euphemism for died

explanation.surface: A burglar breaks in and the lock suddenly gives way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' suggests a door, but it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To trespass is to go on someone else's land without permission.

clue.text: I miss place in resort: it's a field

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone homesick at a holiday resort for their old place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' reads as a holiday destination but means sort again.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialism is a particular area of expertise, a field of study or work.

clue.text: Growing border husband removed remains a border

indicators.note: the husband is taken away from the word

parts.note: a hedge is a border of living, growing shrubs

explanation.surface: A gardener's husband has dug up a hedge, leaving just the boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge is the boundary or rim of something, a border.

clue.text: R&B musician's somewhat unchaste view on derrières

indicators.note: only some of the words' letters are used, a run concealed within them

parts.note: the singer's name runs through the end of unchaste, all of view and on, and the start of derrières

explanation.surface: A singer accused of a rather lewd interest in bottoms.
explanation.definitionFit: The blind singer-songwriter is a giant of rhythm and blues and soul music.

clue.text: Liquid lunch with plenty of character?

definitions.text: Liquid lunch with plenty of character?

parts.words: Liquid lunch with plenty of character?
parts.note: a liquid lunch is usually drinks, and character suggests personality, but here it is soup full of letters, which are characters

explanation.walkthrough: A 'liquid lunch' is slang for a boozy midday session; here it is literally soup, and the characters are pasta letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The soup contains pasta shaped like letters of the alphabet, so it is full of characters.

clue.text: Assuming the worst oddly time-saving

definitions.note: a gerund phrase standing for the noun: the habit of assuming the worst

indicators.note: arranged oddly, in a strange order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pessimist suspicious of a strangely efficient shortcut.
explanation.definitionFit: Negativism is a habitually pessimistic, sceptical attitude that expects bad outcomes.

clue.text: Primarily, what encompasses Senegal, Togo alongside fourteen republics (Ivory Coast, also)?

definitions.text: Primarily, what encompasses Senegal, Togo alongside fourteen republics (Ivory Coast, also)?

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so the first letter of each word is taken

parts.words: what encompasses Senegal, Togo alongside fourteen republics (Ivory Coast, also)
parts.note: the initials of these ten words spell the region's two-word name

explanation.surface: A geography question about the region containing Senegal, Togo, Ivory Coast and other states.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both spells the answer with its initials and describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal, Togo and Ivory Coast are among the countries of the western bulge of the continent.

clue.text: Side in blue seeing confused voter taken in by English Nationalist …

indicators.note: the scrambled word is taken inside the pair of letters
a confused word has its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A political scene: a puzzled voter drawn in by an English nationalist.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is a Liverpool football club that plays in blue.
explanation.definitionFit: The football club is a team famed for its blue shirts.

clue.text: … English Nationalist against adopting promise to be green …

indicators.note: the letter takes in the promise, holding it within

parts.note: VS for versus, against
an IOU is a written promise to pay

explanation.surface: The nationalist turns against a pledge to go green, environmentally.
explanation.definitionFit: Green with envy is the idiom, so green means jealous.

clue.text: … ignoring some, scan ten Nationalists' kit receiving signals

indicators.note: some letters at each end are ignored, leaving a run hidden inside these words

parts.note: the word for the aerial runs from inside scan, through ten, into the start of Nationalists

explanation.surface: Scanning ten nationalists with surveillance equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerial is apparatus that picks up radio or television signals.

clue.text: Sloppily traced over '20s design

indicators.note: something done sloppily is messed up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A careless copy of a design from the twenties.
explanation.walkthrough: O is the cricket abbreviation for over.
explanation.definitionFit: The geometric decorative style flourished in the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Deer eating mushroom recoiled, showing blotch

indicators.note: recoiled, springing back, so the result is read backwards
the deer eat the mushroom, holding it inside

parts.note: elks are large deer
a cep is an edible mushroom, the porcino

explanation.surface: Deer flinch after eating a mushroom, coming out in a rash.
explanation.definitionFit: A speckle is a small spot or mark, a little blotch.

clue.text: Cars that are often seen in Westerns

definitions.meaning: first meaning: saloon cars, closed cars with a separate boot (sedans in the US)

definitions.text: that are often seen in Westerns
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the bars of the Wild West, a staple of cowboy films

explanation.walkthrough: A saloon is the British term for a sedan car.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a closed car body style and a frontier drinking establishment in cowboy films.

clue.text: Activated in potion, life that's everlasting!

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the noun: something that never ends

indicators.note: set into action, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An elixir of eternal life brought to work in a potion.
explanation.walkthrough: In computing this is a sequence of code that repeats without end.
explanation.definitionFit: A program loop with no exit condition runs forever, endless repetition.

clue.text: Record changing dash for cash?

parts.note: turning one word into the other swaps its first letter, so read as wordplay the answer says that letter becomes the other

explanation.surface: Swapping a dash for some money in a changed account.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as three pieces: 'D is C' is what turns dash into cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a gramophone record or other recording.

clue.text: Praiseful verse addressing Archbishop Tutu?

parts.note: O is the vocative, used when addressing someone
Desmond Tutu, shortened to Des

explanation.surface: Verses of praise written to the South African archbishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Odes are lyric poems usually composed in praise of their subject.

clue.text: Flower girl that may be Hazel

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the plant with sword-shaped leaves
third meaning: the coloured part of the eye, which may be hazel

explanation.walkthrough: Hazel looks like another girl's name, but it is an eye colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a flowering plant, a female first name and the coloured ring of the eye.

clue.text: Not the lead horn player getting renewed energy

parts.note: the one behind the leader is second
horn players are in the wind section of an orchestra

explanation.surface: A backup horn player getting a fresh burst of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A second wind is a revival of strength after tiredness.

clue.text: A day after Everyman's age-old booze

indicators.note: the A and day come after the setter's word

parts.note: the setter is Everyman, so Everyman is me

explanation.surface: A day later, the setter is drinking an ancient tipple.
explanation.definitionFit: Fermented honey wine is one of the oldest alcoholic drinks.

clue.text: University becoming independent, raises limits

indicators.note: the university turns into independent, one letter replacing the other

parts.note: to raise a building is to construct it

explanation.surface: A university gaining independence and putting up limits.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrict is to narrow or confine, to restrict.
